_comment: Unit 4's batch. Same rules as voice_curate.json.
This unit's yap is almost entirely the phrase 'the RPC mechanism from Unit 2',
attached to facts that stand on their own - a fact about NFS does not need the
unit that taught RPC in front of it. Two are page directions ('see below', 'the
pages below') and two are the reader being told what to note.

edits.why: the family of properties applied to files is the fact; which unit introduced them is a pointer
edits.old: Transparency in a DFS is the family of properties introduced in Unit 1, applied to files.
edits.new: Transparency in a DFS is the family of properties applied to files.

edits.why: a sentence whose whole content is which other ideas this one is like
edits.old: That is the same idea as the UFID in 4.1.5's architecture and the same idea as the remote object reference in Unit 2.

edits.why: NFS being a set of remote procedures is the fact; that it is an application of Unit 2's RPC is a pointer
edits.old: — so NFS is an application of exactly the RPC mechanism from Unit 2

edits.why: which modules the implementation corresponds to is the course map, not the implementation
edits.old: It does the work of the remote reference and dispatcher modules from Unit 2.

edits.why: 'the Unit 3 problem, offered as middleware' is a pointer wrapped round a one-line description of the service
edits.old: — the Unit 3 problem, offered as middleware

edits.why: a sentence that only says where the same mechanism is taught in full
edits.old: The mechanism — proxy, dispatcher, skeleton, remote reference module and binder, with the at-most-once invocation semantics — is covered in full in Unit 2.2.

edits.why: what the abstraction buys is the fact; the comparison with CORBA and the unit number are commentary
edits.old: It supplies the same thing CORBA does — a programming abstraction over the network, so that one object can call another wherever it runs (Unit 1.3's answer to heterogeneity) — but only inside a Java system.
edits.new: It supplies a programming abstraction over the network, so that one object can call another wherever it runs, but only inside a Java system.

edits.why: the consistency window and the 30 seconds are the fact; 'see below' is a page direction
the two protocols are the choice; 'the choice in the table above' points at the page
edits.old: , and the choice of protocol is the choice in the table above

edits.why: the daemon layout is the content; 'the pages below are' sends the reader to the pictures
edits.old: The pages below are that architecture as the lecture draws it, including the daemon layout of a real cluster: one node running the name-node daemon, and every slave node running a datanode daemon over its own local Linux filesystem, reporting to the master.
edits.new: The architecture includes the daemon layout of a real cluster: one node running the name-node daemon, and every slave node running a datanode daemon over its own local Linux filesystem, reporting to the master.

edits.why: 'note the two distinct purposes' tells the reader what to note; the two purposes are the fact
edits.old: Note the two distinct purposes: checkpointing in normal operation, and a fallback if the primary is lost.
edits.new: Its two purposes are checkpointing in normal operation and a fallback if the primary is lost.

edits.why: a sentence that only says where the same mechanism is taught in full; the paragraph already ends with what the implementation costs
edits.find: The mechanism — proxy, dispatcher, skeleton, remote reference module and binder, with the at-most-once invocation semantics — is covered in full in Unit 2.2.
Two sentences in that list carry the whole design.
edits.why: the two sentences that follow are the design; being told they are the important ones adds nothing
